Every provider names these differently — Acefone calls a number a My Number, Ozonetel calls it a Virtual Number — but they are the same four things, so a new provider reuses this screen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Telephony Account — one per provider tenant. Its webhook token is what authenticates the provider; HMAC and an IP allowlist are optional and off until you turn them on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Numbers (DIDs) — one row per number the business gives you, and the grain it belongs to. A number that is not listed here is dropped. That is what keeps other businesses off a shared provider account out of this CRM. Type the number; pick the grain — it must match the grain on the leads, or a call attaches to nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Agents — only for agents whose provider email is not their CRM login. Staff whose email matches a CRM user resolve on their own and need no row. An unmapped agent never costs you the call; it only leaves the rep blank.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Capture Rules — inside Telephony Settings. Which calls become Call Logs, by direction and channel. Empty captures nothing; telephony is on once you add a rule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every delivery is logged either way. A call that is dropped or declined is recorded in Integration Request with the reason — fix the reason, replay the row, and the call lands.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Accounts", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Routing", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "User Mapping", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Capture Rules", "col": 3}}]
